chunks: O Allah, I call You to witness

against the Quraysh, for they have cut asunder my kinship and over-turned my cup and have joined together to contest a right to which I was entitled more than anyone else. They said to me: 'If you get your right, that will be just, but if you are denied the right, that too will be just. Endure it with sadness or kill yourself in grief.'

key_terms.أَسْتَعْدِيكَ: I call You to witness / I seek Your help against

ai.seo_question: What are the key grievances mentioned in the supplication against the Quraysh?
ai.summary: This du'a, often cited in Shia scholarship as a reflection of Imam Ali’s (AS) political and spiritual stance during the caliphate period, highlights the Quraysh's usurpation of his divinely ordained right to leadership. The imagery of 'overturning the cup' symbolizes the denial of his authority, while the concluding dichotomy of 'patient in sorrow or dying in regret' underscores the theological weight of his endurance amidst political marginalization.
